title: Big Sid Catlett as show drummer
summary: After Kenny Clarke briefly, they hire Sidney Catlett, whom Pillars calls the greatest drummer ever, and take him on a Little Rock tour in 1935.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Uh-huh. The following year Sidney Catlett joined the band. What year -- '35, didn't he?
Believe it was in '35.
I thought he joined the band --
He joined the band a little early, see Kirk didn't finish the season. Wilbur Kirk didn't finish the season.
He joined the band --
IN the Spring of '45 -- '35.
Spring of '35, yes.
Because he was (unintelligible).
That's right. That's right. But before -- before Big Sidney Catlett joined the band, what's the boy's name, out of -- out of -- out of -- out of Pittsburgh? Kenny Clark.
Kenny Clark, yeah.

We sent for Kenny Clark to come out. Kenny Clark came out and joined the band, was a nice drummer. But we had a chance to get Big Sidney Catlett, who was a real great show drummer, not taking anything away from Kenny Clark, so we sent Kenny Clark back to Pittsburgh, and we hired Big Sidney Catlett.

And Big Sidney Catlett, in my opinion, was the greatest drummer ever lived. He could play a floor show so well that the chorus girls would go off and they would turn around and bow to Sidney Catlett. The chorus would bow to the audience and turn around and all of them walk in front of the bandstand and bow to Sidney Catlett, because he made them work. They'd feel so good out there working. He just make them just dance their hearts out. This man was a genius. And it makes a-- everytime I think of his playing, it makes goosepimples, you know, run through my arms. This man was every ounce a genius.
And, he could play fast tempos. You couldn't play too fast for Big Sidney.
And hold them there.

And hold the tempo there, he was a stonewall. He was a great artist. We took Big Sidney on our tour to Little Rock, Arkansas. This was the first time that we had a chance to take our band back home. And we played Little Rock, we played Jackson, Tennessee, we played several towns, you know, that summer. And the people in Arkansas just

went crazy about the band. And Big Sid, his beautiful personality, everybody just loved him. He was a lovable -- a lovable type of guy. He was just a great person. Big Sidney worked that whole summer with us, did he leave before we opened --
No, he didn't leave -- he didn't leave -- he opened the season.
He opened in '35, with us.
Uh-huh.

He opened in '35 with us, but then he -- he left, he had a better job offered him and he left. And, we sent and got Joe Jones. Joe Jones in Sidney's place. Joe Jones worked with us a very fine drummer, you could play shows, he was flashy. But everybody loved Sidney. Especially show people, we all loved him.
